adjudication.answer:
The clearest formulation is that this is a credibility conflict, not an inability to feel love and not primarily a relaxation problem. Relaxation can lower charge, but it cannot alter a track record or settle who was responsible for what. The contempt may be the child, a cynical protector, or both; it should not be classified more confidently than the evidence allows. Its sarcastic line is also a literal question: what will the present-day adult actually do?

The resentful voice also needs a hearing. Before declaring it an inherited parent or an illegitimate critic, determine which age or version it is angry at and what opportunity it believes that version failed to use. A literal small child could not raise itself. An adolescent, younger adult, and persistent present-day child-state involve different degrees of agency.

The next move is for an emerging adult function to hold both sides: hear the exact accusation without endorsing abuse, stop retaliation, allocate responsibility by age and capacity, and complete one observable protective act without demanding gratitude or trust. Borrowed adulthood may be needed here: model the response on a decent adult who can hear 'big whoop,' answer 'fair,' and show up again through repeated action. The action matters, but so do accurate responsibility, repair after internal attacks, and non-defensive listening.

realization.answer:
The ‘big fuckity whoopty doo’ is giving you the right question: what are you going to do for me? That is the credibility problem in one sentence. I would not argue with it. The younger-facing position already has an adverse track record in front of it—the adult outcome itself—while another part of you is blaming some younger version for how that outcome happened. So another vow is almost beside the point.

Before deciding that either side is right, make the accusation specific: separate the literal child, adolescent, younger adult, and present child-state, and identify what you believe the relevant version actually should have done differently with the options it had then. Those versions did not have the same agency.

Then answer ‘what are you gonna do for me?’ literally. Pick one thing in the actual life that makes the relationship more credible and do it. Do not ask the younger side to be impressed. If it says ‘big whoop,’ the adult job may simply be ‘fair’—and then show up again. Relaxation can still lower the charge, but it cannot by itself change an adverse track record or settle responsibility.

And if hearing the sarcasm makes the part attempting the adult role retaliate, that is a good place to borrow adulthood for that side too: model how a decent adult would hear an unimpressed kid without defending its goodness, and practice five percent of that response.
